name: George Alexander
bio: Actor-manager of the St James's Theatre, born George Alexander Gibb Samson (1858-1918) and knighted in 1911. He acted with Irving from 1881, went into management on his own in 1889, and held the St James's from 1891 until his death. He commissioned Lady Windermere's Fan, paying Wilde £50 in advance in January 1890, and produced both it (1892) and The Importance of Being Earnest (1895). Thirteen of Wilde's letters to him survive, from 1890 to four months before Wilde's death; Wilde addressed him throughout as Aleck. At the bankruptcy Alexander bought the acting rights to both plays, made voluntary payments to Wilde afterwards, and left the rights to Wilde's son Vyvyan when he died.
bio_note: Thirteen letters, 1890-1900; dates and name from the editors' note at printed 421. The 1892 rehearsal letters are staging notes ('Lord a's coat is too horsy'), the only human sentence in them being 'I write from bed which accounts for pencil'; their openings run 'Dear Aleck' and 'My dear Aleck'.
